EUDA_CLASSIFICATION.answer: The page says European Union legislation does not establish different classes of narcotic or psychotropic substances, while the EU has a pan-European system to rapidly detect, assess and respond to health and social threats caused by NPS, under the procedures set out in Regulation (EU) 2017/2101. Member States: 'EU Member States classify drugs and precursors according to the three UN Conventions of 1961, 1971 and 1988 (abbreviated below to UN61, UN71 and UN88)', controlling and supervising their legitimate scientific or medical use while taking into account the particular risks to public or individual health.
EUDA_CLASSIFICATION.quote: While European Union legislation does not establish different classes of narcotic or psychotropic substances
EUDA_CLASSIFICATION.note: No published or last-updated date on the page; only years in the text and citations (1961, 1971, 1988, 1997, 11 February 2004, 2017) and 2024/2026 dates in the site navigation. The tool gave the sentences in pieces over three calls; they are joined here. Tool summary only, not verbatim: EU law does set classes for drug precursors, through Regulation (EC) No 273/2004 and Council Regulation (EC) No 111/2005. Verbatim fragment: 'These are the Regulation (EC) No 273/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 February 2004 on drug precursors'.

UK_2017_2103_ART1.answer: 'Drug' means: (a) a substance covered by the 1961 United Nations Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, as amended by the 1972 Protocol, or by the 1971 United Nations Convention on Psychotropic Substances; (b) any of the substances listed in the Annex. Short form: (a) substances under the UN 1961 Single Convention (as amended by the 1972 Protocol) or the UN 1971 Convention on Psychotropic Substances; (b) also any substance listed in the Annex.
UK_2017_2103_ART1.quote: a substance covered by the 1961 United Nations Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs
UK_2017_2103_ART1.note: The tool printed point (a) in two quoted segments split at 'or'; they are joined here. Two calls gave the same wording. Dates printed on the page are not the page's own date: 12 December 2006 (Regulation (EC) No 1920/2006), 13 April 2016 (Interinstitutional Agreement on Better Law-Making), 22 November 2017 (start of the Commission's five-year delegation period).

EURLEX_FD_2004_757.answer: Title, part 1: 'Council Framework Decision 2004/757/JHA of 25 october 2004 laying down minimum provisions'; part 2: 'on the constituent elements of criminal acts and penalties in the field of illicit drug trafficking'. Date of document: 2004-10-25.
EURLEX_FD_2004_757.quote: Council Framework Decision 2004/757/JHA of 25 october 2004 laying down minimum provisions
